name: Gangtok
description: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, set on a ridge with views of Khangchendzonga. Once a transit point for traders travelling between Tibet and India, it is now the state's main administrative and business centre and a base for travel across Sikkim. MG Marg is the town's pedestrian main street.
how_to_reach: Gangtok is reached by road from Siliguri and New Jalpaiguri, with Pakyong airport serving the state and Bagdogra airport in West Bengal as the wider air gateway.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line Permit to enter Sikkim. Carry several copies of your permit, as it is checked at multiple checkpoints; weather-related road closures can occur without notice.

name: Tsomgo Lake
description: Tsomgo Lake, also called Changu Lake, is a high-altitude lake in East Sikkim set in steep, rugged mountain terrain. It is regarded as sacred by the Sikkimese and is known for changing appearance with the seasons, freezing in winter and blooming with flowers in late spring.
how_to_reach: A winding road leads uphill from Gangtok to the lake, which lies in a restricted area beyond the 3rd Mile check post on the Jawaharlal Nehru Road axis. Permitted vehicles can reach the lakeside, and walking or cycling around it is limited.
practical_notes: Tsomgo Lake is in a restricted border area and a special permit is required for all visitors; foreign nationals must be in a group of at least two and apply through a registered travel agency. Carry multiple permit copies and expect weather-related closures without notice.

name: Nathula Pass
description: Nathula Pass is a high mountain pass on the India–Tibet border that was a major trade corridor until 1962. The road to the pass runs through Tsomgo Lake and is among the highest motorable roads, surrounded by alpine flora.
how_to_reach: The pass is reached by road from Gangtok via Tsomgo Lake along the Jawaharlal Nehru Road axis, beyond the 3rd Mile check post. Access is by permitted vehicles arranged through registered operators.
practical_notes: Nathula is a protected border area restricted to Indian nationals on a one-day excursion permit obtained through a registered agency; foreign nationals are not allowed beyond Tsomgo Lake. Photography is prohibited; carry several permit copies and expect weather-related access disruptions without notice.

name: Baba Harbhajan Singh Temple
description: Baba Mandir lies on the road between Nathula and Jelepla Pass and is visited by many devotees and soldiers. It commemorates Sepoy Harbhajan Singh and is believed to have wish-fulfilling powers; visitors leave bottles of water that are collected as holy water on the return journey.
how_to_reach: The temple is reached by road from Gangtok along the Nathula–Jelepla route, passing Tsomgo Lake on the way.
practical_notes: The temple lies inside the protected Jawaharlal Nehru Road border belt; a police permit or Protected Area Permit obtained through a registered agency is required, and foreign nationals cannot travel beyond Tsomgo Lake. Carry multiple permit copies and be prepared for weather-related closures.
address: Baba Harbhajan Singh Temple, Gangtok, Sikkim

name: Rumtek Monastery
description: Rumtek Monastery sits on a hill facing Gangtok and is the seat of the Gyalwa Karmapa of the Kargyu sect of Tibetan Buddhism. It is the largest monastery in Sikkim and houses rare Buddhist religious art objects. The nearby Nehru Botanical Garden has tropical and temperate plants and an orchid greenhouse.
how_to_reach: Rumtek is about 23 km from Gangtok, reached by a road that winds through villages and paddy fields.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit to enter Sikkim and should carry several copies. Follow designated paths, ask before photographing monks or rituals, and check locally for weather-related access changes.

name: Tashi View Point
description: Tashi View Point is a viewpoint reached by road above Gangtok. The district's attraction listing places the Himalayan Zoological Park on the route leading to the viewpoint.
how_to_reach: A road climbs from Gangtok toward the viewpoint; local taxis are available from the town.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies for checkpoints. Roads in the hills can be disrupted at short notice in bad weather, so confirm access locally.

name: Ganesh Tok
description: Ganesh Tok is a viewpoint on a ridge near Gangtok offering a panoramic view of the town with Khangchendzonga and Siniolchu across the hills. A cafeteria at the spot serves tea, coffee and snacks.
how_to_reach: It lies about 7 km from Gangtok and is reached by a short road climb; local taxis are available.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies for checkpoints. Weather can change quickly and views may be obscured or access delayed.

name: Hanuman Tok
description: Hanuman Tok is a temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman on a quiet hilltop about 9 km uphill from Gangtok. The site overlooks peaks around Khangchendzonga and parts of Gangtok, with the nearby Lukshyama royal cremation ground below.
how_to_reach: A road climbs from Gangtok to the hilltop temple; reserved or local taxis can be hired in town.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry multiple copies. Dress modestly at the temple and check locally for weather-related road conditions.

name: Banjhakri Falls
description: Banjhakri Falls is a nature park developed around a waterfall near Gangtok, conceived to showcase Sikkim's flora and the shamanic traditions of the jhakris. It has landscaped trails, footbridges and gazebos, and a pool with a dragon sculpture.
how_to_reach: The falls lie near Ranka, a short drive from Gangtok, and can be covered as part of local sightseeing.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Follow marked trails near the water and check locally for weather-related access changes.

name: Do Drul Chorten
description: Do Drul Chorten is a stupa in Deorali near Gangtok and is listed among the town's primary attractions. Visitors circumambulate the stupa and visit the adjoining monastery.
how_to_reach: The chorten is roughly 1 km from Gangtok in Deorali, near the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology; reserved or local taxis are available.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry copies. Circle the stupa clockwise and ask before taking photographs at religious sites.

name: Enchey Monastery
description: Enchey Monastery is a Buddhist monastery in Gangtok and is listed as a signature attraction of the district. A well-laid road reaches its entrance from Chandmari and the Ridge side, and a footpath with prayer wheels climbs from near Chandmari. Its annual Detor Cham dance festival is held according to the Tibetan lunar calendar.
how_to_reach: The monastery is accessible by road from Chandmari or by a stepped footpath from the Jawaharlal Nehru Marg area; it is about 3 km from the SNT bus station.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry multiple copies. Seek permission before photographing rituals and check locally for access during festival periods or bad weather.

name: Namgyal Institute of Tibetology
description: The Namgyal Institute of Tibetology in Deorali is a research centre for Buddhist philosophy and religion, established in 1958. It holds a large collection of rare Lepcha, Tibetan and Sanskrit manuscripts, statues and thangkas, along with a museum and more than 200 Buddhist icons.
how_to_reach: It lies about 2 km from Gangtok in Deorali, near Tashi Namgyal Memorial Park; local taxis are available from the market and hotels.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies for checkpoints. Follow site rules on photography inside the museum and verify access locally before visiting.
address: Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Gangtok, Sikkim

name: Saramsa Garden
description: Saramsa Garden is a recreational garden and picnic spot between the hills of Pakyong and Gangtok, noted for flowers and medicinal plant species. It hosts the International Flower Festival.
how_to_reach: The garden is about 14 km from Gangtok, reached by the Indira Bypass Road via Ranipool; a taxi ride is the usual way to get there.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Stay on marked paths, avoid littering and check locally for weather-related access changes.

name: Gangtok Ropeway
description: The Gangtok ropeway is a bi-cable zig-back ride that links Deorali with the Tashiling Secretariat area. On a clear day it offers views of the Khangchendzonga range, the town and the valley below; the Ridge Park is a short walk from the upper station.
how_to_reach: Board at the Deorali station within Gangtok; the upper station is near the secretariat and Ridge Park.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. The ride depends on clear weather and may be suspended in poor conditions, so check locally on the day.

name: Lingdum Monastery
description: Lingdum Monastery is a monastery at Ranka near Gangtok, mentioned in the state tourism material alongside Banjhakri Falls as a local attraction. The area is being developed to encourage visitors to extend their stay in Gangtok.
how_to_reach: Ranka lies a short drive from Gangtok; local taxis can be hired for the monastery.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Ask before photographing rituals and check locally for road conditions in the hills.

name: Menmecho Lake
description: Menmecho Lake lies further along the road beyond Tsomgo in East Sikkim and is larger than Tsomgo Lake. It is surrounded by forest and rock formations, is covered with snow from early winter to late spring, and is known for trout.
how_to_reach: The lake is reached by road from Gangtok past Tsomgo Lake; the route continues into the restricted border belt beyond the 3rd Mile check post.
practical_notes: Menmecho lies in the protected Jawaharlal Nehru Road belt beyond Tsomgo, so permits required for Tsomgo and its route apply; foreign visitors must travel in a group through a registered agency. Carry multiple permit copies and expect weather closures without notice.

name: Lachung
description: Lachung is a mountain village in North Sikkim beside the Lachung Chu, surrounded by snow-capped peaks, waterfalls and apple orchards. It has a local self-governing body called the Dzumsa and a prominent monastery that is the focus of religious and cultural life. Lachung is a common overnight stop before Yumthang.
how_to_reach: The road runs from Gangtok through Mangan to Lachung; the nearest airports are Bagdogra and Pakyong and the nearest railway station is New Jalpaiguri.
practical_notes: Lachung is beyond the Phidang/Sankalang/Toong check posts in a protected border area; a Protected Area Permit is required for both Indian and foreign visitors, with foreign permits arranged through registered operators and issued for a limited number of days. Carry copies of the permit and allow for weather-related road closures.

name: Lachen
description: Lachen is a village in North Sikkim at a high altitude, with fewer than 200 houses and a more gradual feel than Lachung. Its residents historically spent summers on alpine pastures near the border, and the village serves as a staging point for travel further north.
how_to_reach: Lachen is reached by road from Gangtok via Mangan, beyond the Phidang/Sankalang/Toong check posts.
practical_notes: The route to Lachen passes into a protected border area; a Protected Area Permit is required for Indian and foreign visitors, and foreign nationals must travel with a registered operator on a permit of limited validity. Carry several permit copies and be prepared for snow or landslip closures.

name: Yumthang Valley
description: Yumthang Valley is a nature sanctuary in North Sikkim with rivers, hot springs and rolling meadows surrounded by Himalayan peaks. It is known for rhododendrons and is popularly called the Valley of Flowers. The Yumthang hot spring sits a short walk from the road across a footbridge on the Lachung River.
how_to_reach: The road runs from Gangtok through Mangan and Lachung to Yumthang.
practical_notes: Yumthang lies in the protected North Sikkim belt beyond the Toong check post; a Protected Area Permit is required and foreign visitors need a permit arranged through a registered operator for a limited stay. Carry multiple permit copies and expect weather-related closures without notice.

name: Gurudongmar Lake
description: Gurudongmar Lake is a high-altitude lake in North Sikkim revered by Buddhists, Sikhs and Hindus and named after Guru Padmasambhava. It remains frozen for much of the year except at one spot said to be blessed by him, and the water is believed to have miraculous powers.
how_to_reach: The road approach is from Gangtok through Mangan and Lachung, continuing north from Thangu toward the lake.
practical_notes: Gurudongmar is deep inside a protected border area beyond the Phidang/Sankalang/Toong check posts; a Protected Area Permit is required for Indian and foreign visitors, with foreign permits arranged through registered operators for a limited stay. Carry several permit copies, travel with a guide, and expect sudden weather closures.

name: Zero Point (Yumesamdong)
description: Yumesamdong, also called Zero Point, is a high barren area further up the valley beyond Yumthang, near the base of the Donkia-la Pass. The rugged, vegetation-free mountains mark the landscape, and a hot spring lies at the spot.
how_to_reach: It is reached by continuing by road past Yumthang along the Lachung valley route from Gangtok via Mangan and Lachung.
practical_notes: Yumesamdong is at the far end of the protected Lachung/Yumesamdong axis beyond the Toong check post; a Protected Area Permit is required and foreign visitors need a permit issued through a registered operator for a limited stay. Carry multiple permit copies and expect access to be halted by weather or border restrictions.

name: Chopta Valley
description: Chopta Valley lies north of Lachen in North Sikkim and is criss-crossed by streams including the Chopta Chu, Thangu Chu and Lassur Chu. The route from Thangu to Chopta Valley and Muguthang is used by visitors who wish to trek and explore the area.
how_to_reach: The approach follows the road from Gangtok through Mangan and Lachen to Thangu; onward travel toward Chopta Valley is on trekking routes.
practical_notes: Chopta Valley is in the remote protected northern belt beyond the Phidang/Sankalang/Toong check posts, so a Protected Area Permit is required and foreign visitors need a permit arranged through a registered operator. Carry several permit copies, travel with a guide, and expect weather-related closures.

name: Thangu Valley
description: Thangu is a small high-altitude village about 30 km north of Lachen, often used for acclimatisation before Gurudongmar Lake or Muguthang. Its alpine meadows, wooden houses and army camps sit beside the Teesta, and the valley is crossed by several streams.
how_to_reach: The road from Gangtok passes Mangan and Lachen to reach Thangu; onward journeys continue by road or on trekking routes.
practical_notes: Thangu lies in the protected northern belt beyond the Phidang/Sankalang/Toong check posts and permits are required for all visitors; foreign permits are issued through registered operators for a limited stay. Carry multiple permit copies and expect snow or road closures at short notice.

name: Phodong Monastery
description: Phodong Monastery stands near Phensang and Labrang on the North Sikkim Highway, around 38 km from Gangtok. It was built in the 18th century by Chogyal Gyurmed Namgyal and belongs to the Kargyupa sect; the original structure was rebuilt while its old murals and frescoes were preserved.
how_to_reach: The monastery is reached along the North Sikkim Highway, on which Phodong, Phensang and Labrang are grouped together.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry several copies. The highway can be affected by landslides and weather, so check access locally before setting out.

name: Labrang Monastery
description: Labrang Monastery is one of three monasteries clustered near Phodong on the North Sikkim Highway. It is noted for its architectural style and rich frescoes covering the interiors. The ruins of Tumlong, Sikkim's third capital, lie between Phodong and Labrang.
how_to_reach: It is reached by road along the North Sikkim Highway, a short distance from Phodong and Phensang.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies for checkpoints. Confirm road conditions locally, as the highway can be disrupted in bad weather, and ask before photographing the frescoes.

name: Seven Sisters Waterfall
description: Seven Sister Falls is a waterfall about 32 km from Gangtok along the National Highway toward North Sikkim. A viewing shed lets visitors take in the cascade and photograph it. The falls are also described as seven waterfalls dropping through dense forest near Dzongu.
how_to_reach: The falls are reached by road from Gangtok toward Phensang along the North Sikkim highway.
practical_notes: The falls lie near the entrance to the protected Dzongu area; if continuing into Dzongu, a Protected Area Permit is required and foreign permits are limited in duration and arranged through registered operators. Carry permit copies and check locally for weather-related road closures.

name: Chungthang
description: Chungthang is a small town where the Lachen Chu and Lachung Chu meet and where the North Sikkim highway splits toward Lachen and Lachung. The valley is considered holy and is associated with Guru Padmasambhava and legends about the origin of the name Demazong.
how_to_reach: It is reached by road from Gangtok via Mangan, at the junction before the roads branch to Lachen and Lachung.
practical_notes: Chungthang sits at the entrance to the protected North Sikkim routes; onward travel toward Lachen, Lachung or Gurudongmar requires a Protected Area Permit, with foreign permits arranged through registered operators. Carry multiple permit copies and expect weather-related closures.

name: Dzongu
description: Dzongu is an area reserved for the Lepcha people, about 70 km from Gangtok in North Sikkim, bordering the Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve. The Lepcha communities live in relative isolation with their own traditions, and the area offers homestays with local families. It is surrounded by views of Khangchendzonga and is rich in flora and fauna.
how_to_reach: Dzongu is reached by road from Gangtok toward Mangan, with the protected area beginning before entry into the reserved belt.
practical_notes: The entirety of Dzongu is a protected area; a Protected Area Permit is required for Indian and foreign visitors, and foreign passes are issued for a limited stay through registered operators. Carry multiple permit copies, travel with a guide, and respect local Lepcha customs and homestay rules.

name: Kabi Lungchok
description: Kabi Lungchok is a sacred spot about 20 km from Gangtok on the way to North Sikkim. Nine stones facing Khangchendzonga mark the place where the Lepchas and Bhutias swore a pact of blood brotherhood in the 15th century.
how_to_reach: The site lies beside the road from Gangtok toward North Sikkim, near Phodong.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry several copies. Treat the stones as a sacred site, keep the area clean, and check locally for road conditions.

name: Khangchendzonga National Park
description: Khangchendzonga National Park is Sikkim's largest wildlife reserve, spread across 1,784 sq km. Mount Khangchendzonga straddles its western boundary and the reserve includes the Zemu Glacier; it is noted for high-altitude ecosystems and rich biodiversity.
how_to_reach: Trek routes enter the park from Yuksom toward Dzongri and Goecha La; other approach routes run from Hilley and Barsey in the west.
practical_notes: The Khangchendzonga National Park axis, including Dzongri, Goecha La, Hilley and Barsey, falls under the protected-area regime; a Protected Area Permit is required and trekking programmes for foreign visitors must be arranged through a registered agency. Carry several permit copies, follow designated trails and expect weather-related closures.

name: Pelling
description: Pelling is about 10 km from Gyalshing and has become the state's second biggest tourist destination after Gangtok. Its main draw is the view of Khangchendzonga and the surrounding ranges, along with easy access to nearby attractions such as Pemayangtse and Rabdentse.
how_to_reach: Pelling is reached by road from Gyalshing, the district headquarters, with public transport available and Bagdogra airport and New Jalpaiguri railway station as the wider gateways.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Roads to and around Pelling can be disrupted by landslides in the monsoon, so check locally before travelling.

name: Pelling Skywalk
description: The Pelling skywalk is a glass-bridge attraction listed with Sanga Choeling Monastery among the signature attractions of Gyalshing district. Visitors come for the glass bridge walk and views of the surrounding hills.
how_to_reach: It is about 10 km from Gyalshing and can be reached by reserved taxi or cab.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry several copies. The bridge operation depends on weather and maintenance, so confirm access locally, and follow the site's safety rules.

name: Yuksom
description: Yuksom means 'meeting place of three lamas' and is of great historical importance: the first Chogyal was crowned there in 1642. The stone throne and the footprint of Lhatsun Chenpo are considered sacred, and the village is a gateway to the Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve and treks toward Dzongri. Dubdi Monastery sits uphill from the village.
how_to_reach: Yuksom is about 33 km from Pelling and 45 km from Gyalshing, with regular taxi services from the district headquarters.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Treks from Yuksom toward Dzongri enter the protected Khangchendzonga park axis and require a Protected Area Permit arranged through a registered agency.

name: Khecheopalri Lake
description: Khecheopalri Lake is a sacred lake in West Sikkim, set between Gyalshing and Yuksom and surrounded by hills. Revered by Buddhists and Hindus and also called the Wishing Lake, it is known for its clear water and calm surface. A trekkers' hut stands near the lake.
how_to_reach: A motorable road connects the lake to Pelling and Gyalshing, and daily jeep services operate from those towns; it is roughly 25 km from Pelling.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry copies. Treat the lake as sacred, avoid littering and check locally for road conditions before travelling.

name: Singshore Bridge
description: Singshore Bridge is a bridge passed on the way to Uttarey from Pelling, Gyalshing or Dentam in West Sikkim. The district page describes it as said to be the second highest bridge in Asia.
how_to_reach: The bridge lies on the road toward Uttarey, reached from Pelling, Gyalshing or Dentam.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies for checkpoints. Stay within designated viewing areas and check locally for weather or road restrictions before travelling.

name: Pemayangtse Monastery
description: Pemayangtse Monastery is one of Sikkim's oldest monasteries, founded by Lhatsun Chempo on a hilltop near Pelling. It belongs to the Nyingma sect and houses a wooden depiction of the Guru's heavenly palace regarded as a masterpiece. The monastery commands wide views over the Himalayan ranges and countryside.
how_to_reach: It lies a short distance before Pelling when approaching from Gyalshing, near a bus stop at Pelling.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Leave a donation if customary, circle shrines clockwise and ask before photographing interiors or rituals.

name: Rabdentse Ruins
description: Rabdentse was the second capital of the Sikkim kingdom after Yuksom and remained the seat of rule until 1814. The ruins lie hidden from the main road, a walk from Pemayangtse Monastery, and offer views across the valley toward the Khangchendzonga range.
how_to_reach: The ruins are about 8 km from Gyalshing, reached by road and then a walk from the entrance or from Pemayangtse Monastery.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Stay on the marked path to the ruins, respect the heritage site and check locally for weather-related access changes.

name: Sanga Choeling Monastery
description: Sanga Choeling Monastery is one of the early monasteries of Sikkim, built in 1697, and sits on the hill opposite Pemayangtse near Pelling. The state tourism page notes a walk of about 40 minutes uphill to reach it.
how_to_reach: It is reached from Pelling by a walk uphill from the hill opposite Pemayangtse; the district also lists the site with the skywalk about 10 km from Gyalshing, accessible by taxi.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. The approach is on foot, so wear sturdy shoes, carry water and ask before photographing inside the monastery.

name: Dubdi Monastery
description: Dubdi Monastery is the first monastery established after the consecration of Sikkim's first Chogyal and stands on a forested hilltop above Yuksom. It can only be reached on foot by a steep climb and has been declared a National Monument under the Archaeological Survey of India.
how_to_reach: The monastery is roughly 2 km uphill from Yuksom and is approached by a trekking path.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. The climb is steep, so go with a guide, stay on the path and check weather conditions before setting out.

name: Tashiding Monastery
description: Tashiding Monastery is a Nyingmapa monastery built on a hilltop near Pelling, overlooking the Rathong and Rangit rivers. It is highly revered in Sikkim, and the Bumchu festival held there marks the ceremonial unveiling of a vessel of holy water. The monastery dates from the 17th century.
how_to_reach: The monastery is reached by road toward Tashiding village, about 50 km from Jorethang, with the final approach on foot.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry several copies. Ask before photographing ceremonies, follow designated paths and check locally for road conditions.

name: Chenrezig Statue
description: Official tourism material provides no separate description of the Chenrezig Statue. The district's primary attraction page identifies the Pelling skywalk and Sanga Choeling Monastery as the signature attractions in this area.
how_to_reach: Reach the Pelling area by road from Gyalshing or Pelling; local paths connect the visitor sites.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Ask before photographing religious figures, follow the site's safety rules and check locally for weather-related access changes.

name: Uttarey
description: Uttarey is a village in West Sikkim approached from Pelling, Gyalshing or Dentam, with the Singshore Bridge on the way. It is known for tranquillity, natural beauty and views of the Himalayan mountains. The area is also a starting point for walks toward Varsey.
how_to_reach: Roads from Pelling, Gyalshing or Dentam lead to Uttarey; the last stretches are served by taxis or jeeps.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Trek routes toward Varsey pass through forest and protected areas, so take a guide, stay on marked trails and expect weather-related delays.

name: Rimbi Waterfall
description: Rimbi is a small village on the Pelling–Darap road where the motorable route ends near the Rimbi power station. The state tourism page lists the spot as a stop on the pilgrimage route toward the third of Sikkim's four sacred caves.
how_to_reach: Reach Rimbi by road from Pelling via Darap; beyond the power station the route continues on foot.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim and should carry several copies. The area is used as a trailhead for longer walks, so take a guide, stay on marked paths and check the weather before setting out.

name: Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
description: Kirateshwar Mahadev Mandir is a Shiva temple at Legship on the left bank of the Rangit River, reached by a foot suspension bridge. It is an important Hindu pilgrimage site with stories from the Mahabharata attached to it. The temple's main festival, Bala Chaturdesi, is observed in December.
how_to_reach: Legship is on the road between Gyalshing and Jorethang; a suspension footbridge leads from the bank to the temple.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. The footbridge can be slippery in rain, so take care, dress modestly and ask before photographing rituals.

name: Gyalshing
description: Gyalshing is the headquarters of West Sikkim and means 'King's Garden'. It is believed to have been the royal gardens attached to the palace at Rabdentse, Sikkim's capital until the late 18th century, and is now the main transit point for the region's tourist sites. Opposite the bazaar is a long mani wall.
how_to_reach: Gyalshing is reached by road and is a hub for taxis and buses to Pelling, Yuksom and other West Sikkim destinations.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies for checkpoints. Mountain roads can be disrupted in bad weather, so confirm onward transport locally.

name: Namchi
description: Namchi means 'top of the hill' and is the headquarters of South Sikkim, set among hills with wide views of snow-capped mountains and valleys. It hosts the Namchi Mahotsav, a tourism, culture and food festival, each October.
how_to_reach: Namchi is about 78 km from Gangtok and is served by Sikkim Nationalised Transport buses and private taxis from Siliguri and other towns.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Check locally for road conditions during the monsoon and respect site rules at pilgrimage places nearby.

name: Samdruptse Hill
description: Samdruptse means 'wish fulfilling hill' and stands above Namchi in South Sikkim. At the top is a 135-foot statue of Guru Padmasambhava, described as the tallest statue of him in the world. The hilltop offers views of Namchi town, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Khangchendzonga and parts of Nepal.
how_to_reach: Samdruptse lies a short distance above Namchi and is reached by road from the town.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Dress modestly at this religious site, follow local photography rules and check access locally in bad weather.

name: Siddhesvara Dhaam (Char Dham)
description: Siddheshwar Dham, or Char Dham, is at Solophok hill about 5 km from Namchi. It centres on a 108-foot statue of Lord Shiva encircled by twelve Jyotirlingams, with representations of the four great Hindu pilgrimage sites. A visit is believed to wash away sins.
how_to_reach: The complex is a short drive uphill from Namchi town.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Follow the dress and photography rules of the pilgrimage site and check locally for access during festivals or bad weather.

name: Ravangla
description: Ravangla is a small town at the base of Maenam Hill and a transit point for tourist destinations in South and West Sikkim. It is a base for treks toward Maenam Hill and Borong and has short nature trails and accommodation. The area is also known for the Buddha Park at nearby Rabong.
how_to_reach: Ravangla is reached by road from Namchi and other South Sikkim towns, with Sikkim Nationalised Transport buses and private taxis available.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Trek routes from Ravangla pass through forest and reserved areas, so take a guide and check weather conditions before setting out.

name: Buddha Park
description: Buddha Park, also called Tathagata Tsal, is near Rabong or Ravangla in South Sikkim. Built between 2006 and 2013, it features a 130-foot Buddha statue consecrated in 2013 and marks the 2550th birth anniversary of Gautama Buddha. The park is on the Himalayan Buddhist Circuit.
how_to_reach: The park is a few kilometres from Ravangla and is reached by road from the town.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Dress modestly, follow the site's photography rules and check locally for weather-related access changes.

name: Tarey Bhir
description: Tarey Bhir is a narrow ridge viewpoint in South Sikkim with sweeping views of river valleys and forests. From the edge one can see the confluence of the Teesta and Rangeet rivers. The district page warns that the ridge can be daunting for visitors who fear heights.
how_to_reach: The viewpoint is about 16 km by road from Namchi, reached by taxi or private vehicle.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Stay back from the ridge edge, do not attempt it in poor weather or low visibility, and follow any local safety barriers.

name: Jorethang
description: Jorethang is an important town in South Sikkim, set on flat land between large hills. It is known for the Jorethang Maghe Mela held each January, a major fair with stalls and cultural events.
how_to_reach: Jorethang is connected by road to Namchi, Siliguri and Darjeeling, with Sikkim Nationalised Transport buses and private taxis.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Roads can be disrupted by landslides in the rains, so check local conditions before travelling.

name: Ralong Monastery
description: Karma Rabdenling Goenpa at Ralong, near Rabong in South Sikkim, is described by the district as the oldest Karma Kagyu monastery in Sikkim. Ralong is also known for hot springs reached by a walk from the monastery.
how_to_reach: Ralong is reached by road from Ravangla or Namchi, with a short walk from the monastery to the hot spring area.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Roads to the monastery can be affected by weather and the walk to the hot springs needs sturdy footwear and a local guide.

name: Doling Monastery
description: Doling Monastery is a Buddhist monastery near Ravangla in South Sikkim. The available official material is limited, so visitors should treat it as a local monastery reached from the Ravangla area.
how_to_reach: The monastery is approached from Ravangla by road and a short walk along the local path.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Ask locally about access, as monastery schedules are not published in the official tourism material, and ask before photographing rituals.

name: Rhenock
description: Rhenock is a town in East Sikkim included in the state tourism department's listed mountain biking routes. The official material gives only route context for Rhenock and nearby areas.
how_to_reach: Rhenock lies on the road route between Rangpo and Rongli and can be reached by road from Gangtok or Pakyong.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry copies. Some routes in the area lead toward protected border belts, so confirm permit requirements locally before riding beyond Rhenock.

name: Zuluk
description: Zuluk is a village on Sikkim's Silk Route circuit in the east, reached through Rongli and Lingtam. The Pakyong district page describes it as a gateway to the circuit with views of the Himalayan landscape.
how_to_reach: The route runs from Gangtok through Rongli and Lingtam to Zuluk; approach roads also connect via Aritar and Lingtam from the Kalimpong side.
practical_notes: Zuluk lies in the protected Lingtam/RN Axis border belt; a police pass or Protected Area Permit is required and permits are issued for a limited stay depending on the itinerary. Carry multiple permit copies, travel with a registered operator and expect weather-related closures.

name: Aritar Lake
description: Lampokari Lake at Aritar in East Sikkim sits on top of a hill, surrounded by greenery, and is considered one of the oldest lakes in the state. It is shaped like a human foot and has been given an artificial embankment for boating. A short trek leads to Mankhim Dara, and Aritar Gumpa is one of the oldest monasteries in Sikkim.
how_to_reach: Aritar is reached by road from Gangtok or Kalimpong, via Rongli or along the Silk Route through Lingtam.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Boating and lakeside activities depend on local conditions, so check on arrival, and ask before photographing at the monastery.

name: Gnathang Monastery
description: Gnathang, also called Nathang, is a high valley on Sikkim's Silk Route circuit in the east, with alpine meadows and mountain views. The district lists Gnathang Valley as an attraction reached along the Silk Route with a pass; no separate official description of the monastery is available.
how_to_reach: Gnathang is reached via the Silk Route from Lingtam, with the route continuing toward Kupup; a pass is required.
practical_notes: Gnathang and the Kupup stretch of the R.N. Road are protected border areas; a police pass covering the route and night stay is required, issued for a limited period depending on the itinerary. Carry multiple permit copies and expect snow or weather-related closures.

name: Rinchenpong
description: Rinchenpong is a tourist spot in West Sikkim known for mountain views, sunrise and sunset, flora and fauna, and the heritage of Resum Monastery. It sits at about 5,576 ft and has rich forests and scope for short treks. The area is also historically significant.
how_to_reach: Rinchenpong is about 40 km from Jorethang, reached by road from Jorethang or other West Sikkim towns.
practical_notes: Foreign visitors need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim; carry several copies. Roads in the area can be affected by landslides, so check locally and take a guide for short treks.

name: Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary
description: Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary lies on a ridge in West Sikkim between Singalila National Park and the Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve. It is known for rhododendrons that bloom in March and April, along with pine, magnolia and oak. The sanctuary supports bird watching, hiking and village walks.
how_to_reach: A hike of about 5 km from Hilley leads to the sanctuary; Hilley is the last motorable point on the approach from Gangtok or Soreng.
practical_notes: Barsey falls in the protected Khangchendzonga National Park axis covering Hilley and Barsey, and visitors must obtain a permit at the forest check post; foreign nationals also need an Inner Line or Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim. Carry multiple permit copies, do not pluck flowers, and expect weather-related closures.
